thread.title: Tech Firms Lead Stock Buybacks In Second Quarter| Investor's Business Daily

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: Tech Firms Lead Stock Buybacks In Second Quarter| Investor's Business Daily
text:
Technology companies led all other industry sectors in stock buybacks among companies in the S&P 500 in the second quarter, with Apple ( AAPL ) again topping the list, said a report issued Monday.
X
Technology companies spent $71.5 billion on stock buybacks in the second quarter, up 13% from the prior quarter and 159% from the year-ago period. The tech sector represented 37.5% of total buybacks in the S&P 500, according to the report from S&P Dow Jones Indices .
Stock buybacks, or share repurchases, are a popular way to return capital to shareholders. They tend to boost a stock and per-share earnings due to lower share counts.
"For the second half of 2018, indications are strong for increased corporate expenditures in both buybacks and dividends, with annual records for both," said Howard Silverblatt, senior index analyst at S&P Dow Jones Indices, in prepared comments.

Top 5 In Stock Buybacks Apple again led in buybacks, spending $21.9 billion in the second quarter. The quarter was its second highest historically.
Apple was followed by pharmaceutical company AbbVie ( ABBV ) at $7.5 billion, then Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) at $6.1 billion. Cisco was followed by Union Pacific ( UNP ) at $5.5 billion, then Broadcom ( AVGO ) at $5.4 billion.
Following the tech sector in buybacks was the financials sector, then health care and industrial.
Shares of Apple closed at 220.79, up 1.4% on the stock market today . AbbVie closed at 93.43, up 1.3%. Cisco ended the day at 48.44, down a fraction. Union Pacific fell 1% to close at 163.18.
Other tech companies making the top 20 list overall included Oracle ( ORCL ), Intel ( INTC ), Facebook ( FB ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ).
